subject.title: [Refactor] Extract canonical configuration validation from core to plugin boundaries

question: Should OpenClaw retain manifest-only cold configuration validation, or intentionally add boot-time runtime interrogation of installed plugins for schema composition?
rationale: Current main already uses plugin-owned manifests, while the proposed executable interrogation model changes startup, failure-isolation, and trust boundaries; repository evidence cannot establish that direction without maintainer intent.

options.title: Retain manifest-first validation
options.body: Require a concrete residual core-owned schema and move only that schema into existing manifest metadata without loading plugin runtime code.

options.title: Sponsor runtime schema interrogation
options.body: Define a new plugin API and startup lifecycle contract for executable schema discovery, including failure isolation and compatibility behavior.

recommendation.title: Retain manifest-first validation
recommendation.body: Require a concrete residual core-owned schema and move only that schema into existing manifest metadata without loading plugin runtime code.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work and review activity span the manifest, plugin lifecycle, and architecture boundaries implicated by this decision.
